publicReview.corrections.revenueSummary: Sale credits and split-wallet code exist; royalty activation and the complete launch payment path remain unfinished.
publicReview.corrections.roleIntroductio: Core is the main contract for token identity and ownership. Separate contracts handle tasks such as minting, payments, and artwork records. People have different permissions to use and configure them.
publicReview.corrections.curationIntrodu: TDH (Total Days Held) is 6529's holding-based score. Its calculation and community selection happen outside the Stream contracts.
publicReview.corrections.signerEpoch: The older Drop code checks that a permission has not expired, been cancelled, or already been used. It also checks the signer's version number, called an epoch. Changing that number invalidates older permissions.
publicReview.corrections.mintHeading: ## Minting logic and its blocked connection
publicReview.corrections.randomnessCommi: **Built in the permanent Core:** Core records which entropy coordinator is selected when a token is minted. This is the contract responsible for coordinating its random result. Core passes a mint commitment, a fingerprint of the mint inputs, to that coordinator; it does not store the commitment itself. **Agreed but unfinished:** the complete service still needs the coordinator, provider, reveal funding, and recovery path connected and tested.
publicReview.corrections.metadataIntrodu: Core records the token's identity and fixed token data. Metadata is the information used to describe and display it, such as its name and artwork location. Separate contracts store those records; a router is the contract Core asks for the current display information.
publicReview.corrections.governanceIntro: Core's code cannot be swapped after deployment. Separate contracts can be replaced through approved governance actions: each change must follow the required permissions, checks, and waiting periods.
publicReview.corrections.governancePoint: A pointer is Core's stored reference to another contract. Changing it requires checks against the registered contract and its expected identity. Freezing a pointer prevents later replacement of that reference; it is separate from freezing a collection.
publicReview.corrections.readinessSpecif:
The agreed design requires artist approval, collaborator and estate protections, correct payment for each mint, connected launch components, and replacements that preserve obligations and history.

The specification inventory still lists Draft documents. Accepted design decisions do not make those documents Final or prove that the code meets them. The specification policy blocks deployment until the governing specifications reach Final; permanent interfaces and rules must be completed before Core is deployed. See the [specification policy](https://github.com/6529-Collections/6529Stream/blob/92ea123380917032f01aae09691141a2a72df935/docs/spec-policy.md).
publicReview.corrections.mintComponents: The permanent Core, mint manager, and ledger are implemented separately. The real manager and ledger cannot yet pass Core's installation checks, so their connection needs fixing and testing together.
publicReview.corrections.mintExecution: The manager's execution logic checks its phase and gates, records used allowances and claims in the ledger, then asks Core to mint. The real manager cannot yet be installed into permanent Core, so this describes implemented logic whose connection is blocked.
publicReview.corrections.lifecycleFreeze: Burn blocking is a separate irreversible step after closure. It must happen before Core freeze, but the two actions can execute in the same transaction once the required governance conditions are met. Freeze locks the Core collection boundary; it does not by itself freeze every external artwork record or keep a file online.
publicReview.corrections.artistRoyalties: Stream is designed to report royalty instructions to marketplaces. This candidate cannot install its royalty resolver, so the Core lookup currently returns zero. This connection must be completed before deploying permanent Core. Even then, royalty information cannot force a marketplace to pay.
publicReview.corrections.managerRole: Implemented phase and ledger checks prepare mint requests. The real manager cannot yet pass permanent-Core installation checks.
publicReview.corrections.artistConnectio: The newer artist archive stores evidence and the registry directory identifies contracts. Neither is the completed authority system, and Core's artist-registry connection is currently disabled. ADR 0023's division of artist responsibilities remains proposed.
publicReview.corrections.managerChecks:
**Built separately; connection blocked:** the manager and ledger contain mint execution and accounting logic, but neither implements the ERC-165 interface response required for installation into permanent Core. Their custom marker methods do not satisfy that check. The real registry, governed installation, manager, ledger, and Core still need to work together.

The manager's logic checks the phase, caller, token batch, and required gates.
publicReview.corrections.mintRemaining: Fixing module installation will not by itself complete artist consent or a paid sale. Shared counters across phases, global counters, and successor continuity also remain unfinished.
publicReview.corrections.freezeOrder: Burn blocking is a separate irreversible action after closure. Burns must be blocked before Core is frozen. These actions can happen in the same transaction once the required governance conditions are met; Core does not require an extra block between them. The specification also permits ordered artwork finalization in that batch when all of its separate conditions are satisfied.
publicReview.corrections.finalityConnect: The source contains a finality registry and a read adapter that combines Core facts with collection metadata. The real registry also lacks the interface response required for installation into Core. Its scheduling, veto, and execution checks are implemented separately from that blocked connection.
publicReview.corrections.royaltyLookup:
**Lookup code exists; activation is blocked:** Core has a royaltyInfo function, but its royalty-resolver interface is unresolved and installation is rejected. Ordinary configuration of this candidate therefore leaves the lookup at no receiver and zero royalty. This must be resolved before deploying permanent Core; adding a new resolver afterward cannot repair a disabled Core connection. The separate primary-revenue resolver is not the complete royalty system.

Do not describe this Core as reporting a universal fixed 6.9% royalty; that belongs to the legacy Core.
publicReview.corrections.withdrawalLimit: Fixed-price and auction credits are separate balances in separate contracts. A failed withdrawal rolls back that attempt and preserves its credit, but that does not guarantee a working recovery route. Rotating the curator pool can strand older reserve credits until configuration is restored. Auction bidder refunds are also separate from seller proceeds; the winning bid is not an outbid-refund credit.
publicReview.corrections.assetDeprecatio:
The split factory and wallets represent fixed recipients and shares. The resolver selects revenue policies, and the settlement contract provides a separate payment entry point. These components need to be connected to the actual sale path; merely deploying a wallet does not route sale money into it.

The specification requires eligible existing balances to remain withdrawable when a payment token is deprecated, meaning retired from new use. The current split wallet instead blocks those withdrawals until the token is reactivated. Treat the required withdrawal protection as unfinished.
publicReview.corrections.auctionLimits:
If there are no bids, the token returns to an ordinary poster wallet. A contract poster receives a claim right so it can choose a receiving address. Cancellation is limited to the pre-bid case and the permitted poster/admin callers. A failed safe transfer rolls back that cancellation.

The winner has no equivalent alternate-recipient recovery. If a winning contract cannot receive the NFT, settlement fails and both the NFT and winning payment remain held. The no-bid return path does not solve that case.

The older auction also reads mutable payment splits at settlement: an authorized admin can change who gets paid after a funded bid. A zero-reserve auction accepts zero-value bids that can extend its timer, and rounding can let a tiny outbid equal the previous bid. These are limitations of the retained older code, not evidence about unimplemented replacement sale contracts.
publicReview.corrections.randomnessGas:
These integrations belong to the older Core flow. The retained sale rehearsal uses a test-only legacy Core and wires those randomizers there. A passing legacy callback is not proof of a complete reveal connection for the permanent Core.

The legacy VRF callback defaults to 40,000 gas. That budget needs testing with the intended provider: if the callback runs out of gas before saving the seed, the local retry cannot recover it. The post-processing retry only covers results already accepted. The production provider needs measured callback limits and a tested recovery path.
publicReview.corrections.readinessMint: - The manager and ledger implement ADR 0018's batch operation roots, per-token identities, and replay accounting, but the real modules fail permanent-Core installation checks.
publicReview.corrections.readinessRoyalt: - Core has royalty lookup code and restricted metadata refresh helpers. Its royalty-resolver connection is disabled, leaving the lookup at zero; the artist-registry connection is disabled too.
publicReview.corrections.readinessPriori: First prove real module registration and governed installation into permanent Core, then trace one complete artist-approved paid mint. Check rollback and replay across manager, ledger, payment, and Core. Keep legacy rehearsals separate from permanent-Core evidence. Check failed NFT delivery, old-credit withdrawals, changed auction splits, and provider callback gas before relying on the older flows. Exercise closure, burn blocking, finality, emergency stops, and module replacement with their exact authorities.
publicReview.corrections.overviewMint: Parts of that journey are built separately. The real manager and ledger cannot yet pass installation into permanent Core. Artist approval, royalty activation, and the complete sale and payment connections still need work. The retained signed-sale rehearsal uses a test-only legacy Core; it does not prove that the permanent-Core journey works.
publicReview.corrections.overviewMintLin: identity, supply, and the blocked mint connection.
